rules.fix: Move db.add/add_all/merge/flush/refresh/delete into the model's crud.

A leading `_` marks an implementation detail: a `_` name is private to its module, and a `_` module or package is private to its parent package and that package's children. Code outside (a test included) that imports it, patches it, or reaches it as an attribute or by a string depends on that detail, so the detail can no longer change without breaking that code. Decide what the private thing is (the playbook's one question): an implementation detail, so test the public behaviour that runs it and fake only what crosses the app's boundary (HTTP, clock, storage); a real capability, so extract it to a public service and test that; or shared data or config wearing an underscore, so make it public where it belongs. Never make it public just so a test can reach it, and never swap the import for a string-path patch, an attribute access or a getattr: that is the same coupling, hidden.
rules.example:
red     from app.services.core._oidc import _pkce_pair
        monkeypatch.setattr("app.services.core._oidc._discover", fake_discover)

        def test_pkce_pair():
            verifier, challenge = _pkce_pair()
            assert challenge == s256(verifier)

clears  from app.services.core.auth import build_login_redirect   # the public seam

        def test_login_redirect_carries_an_s256_challenge(httpx_mock):
            httpx_mock.add_response(url=DISCOVERY_URL, json=DISCOVERY)  # fake the IdP, not _oidc
            url = build_login_redirect(state="s")
            q = parse_qs(urlparse(url).query)
            assert q["code_challenge_method"] == ["S256"]

The PKCE coverage survives: it is asserted through the URL the user is sent to, which is
the behaviour that matters, and _oidc can now be rewritten without touching a test.

rules.fix: Register every PUBLIC component macro in the component index (the catalogue agents discover macros from) — or _-prefix it if it's an internal helper. The library is the ONE branded source of a component; an unregistered macro is invisible, so the next agent reinvents it (a 'generic button' when btn_* already exist). Declare the registry with [components].index (a file, a dir, or a LIST of them if the library is split by audience); missing one → create it. A macro is registered when the index names it IN CODE, tied to its file — `{% from "macros/x.html" import name %}` (then show it: `{{ name(…) }}`), or `{% import "macros/x.html" as x %}` and `x.name(…)`. A mention in prose, a table of names, a comment or a CSS class is not a registration. Point at the ACTUAL catalogue(s), never a broad parent dir — a broad parent makes a macro merely USED beneath it count as registered (a false green). Never a generic/parallel macro. See --playbook component-macros.

the harness isolates by holding ONE connection and rolling it back (tests/conftest.py:202), so a pooled test engine cannot work here — each pytest-asyncio test gets its own loop and a pooled connection belongs to the loop that opened it. **This INERT is the correct END STATE for such a harness, not a todo.** Do NOT migrate to DELETE/TRUNCATE-per-test to satisfy this rule: luxlint's test.no_handrolled_cleanup exists to red exactly that, and rollback isolation is the better pattern (faster, no table-ordering bugs, nothing to forget). An earlier version of this message named that migration as the prerequisite and was wrong — it pointed at something another fleet guard forbids. Measured, pursuing pooling here costs you: 0 failures on NullPool, 139 pooled, 366 pooled+dispose. And you lose nothing in DETECTION — the cross-session visibility class this rule guards is caught by durability locks that read on a SEPARATE connection, which works whatever the pool class. Pool the APP engine (fw.dev_prod_pool_parity); leave the test engine alone.

A registry-qualified tag you BUILD must also be PUSHED (never split them — a built-but-unpushed deployable name is a local-only image that a prune silently deletes), and a verification image must be BARE (`$(notdir $(IMAGE_NAME)):test`) so it cannot be pushed or mistaken for a deployable. See --doc FLEET-BUILD-DEPLOY-STANDARD.

pin an immutable identifier in `.env.<env>` (compose) or the overlay's `images: newTag:` (kustomize): `sha-<commit>` (every build, no ceremony — the sha is already computed for BUILD_COMMIT) or `TAG=<version>` for a cut release. A moving tag cannot be a deployment record: you cannot say which bits are running and you cannot roll back to them. `luxarch --emit image-block` prints the canonical scheme, where `:dev` survives only as a human-readable alias nothing pins.
